The Quiet Lighthouse

Lighthouses have guided ships safely to shore for more than two thousand years, long before radar or satellites existed.

The keeper of the northern light climbed three hundred steps every evening to trim the lamp and polish the great glass lens.

Today most lighthouses are automated, yet sailors still rely on their steady beam when storms close in and the coast disappears.

Each tower has its own flash pattern, which lets a captain identify the exact stretch of coast from many miles away.
